resources.title: How to Choose the Right Workshop
resources.excerpt: A simple way to compare workshop formats, outcomes and the kind of practice you need next.

sections.title: Start with something you want to do
sections.text: Choose an outcome before choosing a topic. Building a small website, testing a prototype or writing a campaign brief gives you a clearer target than simply learning more about a subject.

sections.title: Check the level and the format
sections.text: Read the prerequisites and look for time to practice. A beginner session should explain its tools and starting point. A more advanced session should be clear about the knowledge you need to bring.

sections.title: Make room for follow-through
sections.text: Set aside time after the workshop to repeat the exercise without the walkthrough. Save your questions and notes, and decide on one small change you can make to the project yourself.

resources.title: Skills Worth Learning in 2026
resources.excerpt: The practical skills that help students and early-career professionals stay useful as work changes.

sections.title: Choose skills that connect to your work
sections.text: A useful learning plan starts with the problems you encounter. If you work with information, practice organizing and checking it. If you build products, practice making small prototypes and explaining your decisions.

sections.title: Practice judgment alongside tools
sections.text: For AI, learn to frame a task and verify an answer. For web development, practice accessibility and debugging alongside coding. For design and marketing, get comfortable testing assumptions with the people you are trying to reach.

sections.title: Show the work
sections.text: Keep a short record of what you tried, what changed and what you would do next. A modest finished project with a clear explanation is useful evidence of progress.

resources.title: How Practical Learning Improves Skill Development
resources.excerpt: Why trying, sharing and getting feedback often beats another hour of passive content.

sections.title: Turn an explanation into an exercise
sections.text: After watching a demonstration, try a small version yourself. The gaps you notice while doing the task give you specific questions to ask and a useful starting point for more practice.

sections.title: Get feedback on something concrete
sections.text: Share a draft, prototype or working example. Ask a focused question: is the flow clear, does the result solve the problem, or where does the explanation become difficult to follow?

sections.title: Repeat with one change
sections.text: Adapt the exercise to a different situation. Change the input, audience or constraint, then explain why your approach still works or why it needs to change. Keep both versions so you can see your progress.
